newsitem.title: USA: U.S. West Coast late prods notionally unchanged.
newsitem.headline: U.S. West Coast late prods notionally unchanged.

text.p: U.S. West Coast product prices were notionally unchanged in thin late trade, as players waited out volatile NYMEX movements.
Sellers stuck to their offers, watching from the sidelines to see if heating oil fluctuations would force them to cut prices.
The front-month contract peaked at 74.40 cents, then settled down 1.51 cents at 71.56 cents a gallon.
"The lower we go the easier it is to test this uptrend line," one trader said, referring to the relative bullishness seen since July in the markets.
Early fourth quarter refinery margins slid 21 percent versus last quarter on the West Coast, an analyst report said on Wednesday.

Low sulphur diesel in Los Angeles stayed 71/71.50 cents a gallon. Jet fuel bids held at 67.50 cents a gallon, with offers flat at 68 cents. CARB diesel in L.A. was notionally unchanged at 83/84 cents, with November parcels heard bid at 79 cents.

Los Angeles CARB regular gasoline was unchanged at 67/68 cents a gallon, after a flat Tuesday. Conventional regular gasoline in L.A. stayed 62/63 cents. --David Brinkerhoff, Los Angeles bureau +1 213 380 2014
